_comment: EXAMPLE -- the trust policy for the role named in hosted-zones.json under
roles.external_dns. Not applied by this repo; the customer creates it in
the account that owns the zone.
Different mechanism from cert_manager. external-dns runs INSIDE the
cluster, so it uses EKS Pod Identity: the pod identity agent obtains
credentials for this role and hands them to the external-dns pod. Nothing
outside the cluster assumes it, which is why there is no cross-account
sts:TagSession is required alongside sts:AssumeRole -- Pod Identity tags
the session with the cluster, namespace and service account, and the
AssumeRole call fails without permission to set those tags.
The association is made separately, per cluster, with
eks:CreatePodIdentityAssociation naming this role, the namespace and the
service account -- so the trust policy needs no cluster-specific detail.
Permissions on this role are the customer's decision. external-dns needs
route53:ChangeResourceRecordSets on the zone it manages, plus
route53:ListHostedZones and ListResourceRecordSets. Unlike cert_manager it
does need to write A and CNAME records, so it cannot be constrained to TXT.
